title: The guest journey: from first click to farewell
vimeoName: Module 5 - The guest journey: from first click to farewell

segments.text: Every guest who arrives at Crevoral is on a journey that started long before the M501 brought them to our gate and finishes long after they leave.
In this module, I want to walk that old journey with you, stage by stage, because each of you owns a piece of it and it helps enormously to see the whole.
Stage one, the dream. Before anything, someone is at home, in Lisbon, in Munich, in London, scrolling, dreaming of a Skype.
They see our photographs, the houses among the trees, the long table, the coastline. At this stage, we've made a promise.
Everything our marketing shows, the aesthetics, the calm, the farm, is a promise that the operation, meaning you, will have to keep.
I take this seriously. We never promise what we can't deliver. Our photos are real, our words are real, which means the bar is exactly where it should be.
Reality has to match the dream. That's hard. That's also the job.
Stage two, booking and the time before. Someone chose us over hundreds of alternatives.
From that moment, they're already our guests, months before arrival. Every email answered quickly and warmly.
Every question about cuts or dogs or dietary restrictions handled with care builds their confidence that they chose well.
And remember, we favor direct bookings.
When guests book directly through creveral.pt, more of the value stays in the circle, and we can take better care of them.
When you talk to potential guests, that's always the best pass for them and for us.
Stage three, the arrival. Two and a half hours from Lisbon, 90 minutes from the Algarve.
Guests arrive tired, sometimes lost, often with kids who've had enough.
The first 15 minutes at creveral set the emotional tone for the entire stay.
I'd honestly say the first 15 minutes are worse than the next three days.
A genuine welcome. A cold drink. A calm, unhurried explanation of the house and the property.
Never a bureaucratic check-in. The message underneath every word and gesture must be, you made it.
You can let go now.
Stage four, the first morning.
This is where creveral really begins.
The guest wakes without an alarm for the first time in months.
Rosemary in the air.
Breakfast.
And our breakfast is a statement of identity.
Housemade breads, our preserves, local cheeses, eggs laid that morning, cooked how they want them.
The first morning is when the guest decides, mostly unconsciously, whether this place is what it promised.
Make the first morning perfect and the whole stay tilts toward joy.
Stage five, the days.
And here, the guiding principle is freedom.
Some guests want everything.
Surf at Carvalel, horseback riding on the coast, the boat on the Mirra River, hiking to Zambujera, yoga, massage, the thermal circuit on the wellness deck in the pines.
Others want the precise opposite.
Pool, book, wine, repeat.
Both are perfect stays.
Our art is reading which guest is which, offering without pushing, informing without pressuring.
And for families, the kids, pizza classes, the animals, the eggs in the morning, the bikes.
A child who feeds a goat at eight in the morning has already made the families holiday.
Children are not an inconvenience at Creveral.
They're the guests whose memories last longest.
Stage six, the friction points.
Let me be honest about where the journey typically strains because pretending otherwise doesn't help you.
Housekeeping timing, guests are out, guests are in.
Coordinating is genuinely hard.
Restaurant capacity on peak nights.
The distances on the property, beautiful, but a long walk with luggage in August heat, needs help offered proactively.
Weather, an Atlantic storm in April can bruise a beach holiday, and that's exactly when we shine or fail.
The heated indoor pool, the saunas, the fireplace, the long lunch.
A rainy day at Creveral should be remembered as the coziest day of the trip, not the lost one.
Know these friction points.
Own them before the guest feels them.
Stage seven, the farewell.
Departures matter as much as arrivals.
The psychology is real.
People remember peaks and endings.
Never let a departure be reduced to an invoice.
A warm goodbye, a genuine comeback, maybe something small from the shop or the farm for the road.
The last image in the rearview mirror should feel like leaving a friend's house.
Stage eight, after.
The journey doesn't end at the gate.
There's the review they'll write, and reviews are the modern word of mouse.
They decide whether the next dreamer in Munich clicks on us or on someone else.
There's the memory that ripens over months, and there's the return.
Our best guests come back year after year, and some have become genuine friends of the house.
That's the real measure of everything I've described.
Not whether they were satisfied, whether they'll be back.
Here's the mental exercise I want to leave you with.
Whatever your role, locate yourself on this journey.
Which stages do you touch?
Housekeeping touches four and five, every single day.
Reception touches nearly all of them.
The kitchen owns Stage Four's magic.
Maintenance quietly protects every stage at once.
Nobody at Creviral is outside the journey.
Once you see the map, you'll never again think of your work as tasks.
It's a relay, and the betton is the guest's trust.
Next module, the houses, the farm, and the standards we keep.
